title: Evaluating Language Models
blurb: How the field decides whether a model is any good — and the steady realisation that static benchmarks are not enough.

anchors.note: 57 subjects of multiple-choice knowledge. Flawed and saturating, but still the number everyone quotes.
Functional correctness on real programs instead of text overlap. Introduced pass@k.
204 tasks built to be hard for current models, and an honest look at where scaling does not help.
Argues evaluation should be multi-metric and transparent, not one accuracy number. As much a methodology paper as a benchmark.
Using a strong model as the judge, with the correlation study to justify it — and the biases that come with it.
Pairwise human preference at scale. The current answer to benchmark saturation.
